title: Creative
purpose: When ads are tiring and I have to decide what to make next, open Creative to see which ideas sell and why, and keep a steady supply of ads that buy the most gross profit.
fires: The agency's creative deck, the Friday 'what is working' call, the folder of 200 unnamed files, and gut calls on which ad to kill.
not_for: A store spending under a few thousand dollars a month on ads, where 2 or 3 good ads a month and a weekly look at the ad account are enough.

jobs.job: When Monday numbers land, tell me which ads are winning and losing and why, broken into hook, message, proof and offer, so I stop feeding ads that look busy and do not sell
jobs.circumstance: Monday morning; 40 live ads, spend up, and the media buyer waiting to know what to scale and what to cut

progress.functional: each ad marked scale, watch or cut, with the part that made it win or lose
progress.emotional: stop the dread of guessing with real money
progress.social: give the media buyer and the agency a clear call; look in command of the account

jobs.hire_today: the agency's Monday call, the media buyer's read of Ads Manager, or gut
jobs.fire: the Monday call and the Ads Manager scroll

forces.push: 45 percent of spend sits on ads above target cost per purchase
forces.pull: a ranked list of winners and losers, each with a written reason
forces.habit: the agency has always made this call
forces.anxiety: what if I cut an ad that was about to turn

jobs.little_hire: every Monday, and any day spend jumps

watch.metric: share of spend on ads at or under target cost per purchase, 7 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 45 percent of spend on ads above target. After: 70 percent at or under target within 14 days, each winner and loser with a written reason.
jobs.not_for: a store spending under a few thousand dollars a month, where a weekly look at Ads Manager is enough

jobs.job: When a strong ad's results slide, tell me whether it is worn out or just starved of budget or new people, so I do not kill a winner or keep feeding a dead one
jobs.circumstance: The best ad's click rate is down 30 percent in 10 days, and the buyer wants to switch it off

progress.functional: a call on each sliding ad: worn out, underfunded, or a targeting problem
progress.social: back the media buyer's call with a reason

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer's eye on the click rate

forces.push: winners get cut too soon and tired ads run too long
forces.pull: each sliding ad checked against whether its audience is still growing
forces.anxiety: what if the read is wrong and I kill the best ad

jobs.little_hire: any day a top ad's results slide

watch.metric: click rate drop from the ad's own peak, against reach growth this 7 days versus the prior 7
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: cost per purchase on the top 5 ads, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of the top 5 ads lost 30 percent of their click rate with flat reach. After: refreshed within 7 days; cost per purchase back under target.
jobs.not_for: a store running only 2 or 3 ads, where every ad is visible every day anyway

jobs.job: When an ad goes out with a health claim, fake scarcity or a face we have no right to use, catch it before launch, so I do not get the account restricted
jobs.circumstance: 20 new ads go live Friday, and one says 'cures foot pain'

progress.functional: every ad checked against approved claims, real offers and rights before launch
progress.emotional: stop the fear of the rejection email
progress.social: keep the account in good standing

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer, after the rejection

forces.push: 5 ads rejected last month for health claims
forces.pull: a pre-launch check against the brand record
forces.anxiety: what if the check blocks a good ad over a close call

watch.metric: ads rejected or limited, count, 30 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: spend lost to rejected ads, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 ads rejected last month for health claims. After: 0, with every claim checked before launch.
jobs.not_for: a store in a category with no claim rules, selling plain goods

jobs.job: When the 2 or 3 ads carrying the account start to tire, have enough new ones ready to take over, so I do not see costs jump the week they fade
jobs.circumstance: Two ads take most of the spend, both are 8 weeks old, and nothing new is ready

progress.functional: a steady monthly flow of new ads, sized to how fast ours wear out
progress.emotional: stop the fear of the cliff
progress.social: the team knows what it has to ship each month

jobs.hire_today: an agency or in-house team shipping when they can
jobs.fire: making ads only when results fall

forces.push: 6 new ads last month against a plan of 20
forces.pull: a monthly count against plan, with the gap named early
forces.habit: we make ads when we need them
forces.anxiety: what if volume means worse ads

watch.metric: new ads launched this month against plan
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level, with the creative plan

drives.metric: cost per purchase, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6 new ads last month against a plan of 20. After: 20 a month on time, 4 of them new ideas.
jobs.not_for: a store whose ads last for months and rarely tire

jobs.job: When I pay a creative agency every month, tell me how many of their ads made money, so I know if the retainer earns its keep
jobs.circumstance: Retainer renewal next week; the agency's deck shows 30 ads made and 'strong engagement'

progress.functional: each agency ad with its spend, results and verdict, and the cost per ad that paid back
progress.social: hold the agency to account with numbers they cannot argue with

jobs.hire_today: the agency's own report

forces.push: $8,000 a month with no clear return
forces.pull: one line: ads made, ads that paid back, cost per winner
forces.anxiety: what if it shows my own hire was wrong

watch.metric: agency ads that reached a scale verdict within 14 days, share, 90 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level, with the brief log

drives.metric: creative cost per winning ad, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 30 agency ads a month, value unknown. After: 3 of 30 won; cost per winner $2,700; the brief changed.
jobs.not_for: a store that makes its own ads in house

jobs.job: When a proven winner fades, get fresh openings on the same body this week before paying for a new idea, so I get back to target at a fraction of the cost
jobs.circumstance: The old winner runs at $41 per purchase against $26 at its peak

progress.functional: new first 3 seconds on a proven ad body, tested fast

jobs.hire_today: an editor recutting when asked

forces.push: new ideas cost weeks and money; the proven body sits idle
forces.pull: 4 new openings on the old body within a week
forces.anxiety: what if new openings just delay the fall

jobs.little_hire: each time a top ad slides

watch.metric: cost per purchase of refreshed versions against the original ad's best 14 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: cost per purchase, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the old winner at $41 against $26 at its peak. After: 4 new openings; the best at $28.
jobs.not_for: a store whose ads are all stills with no body to reuse

jobs.job: When a sale ends or a color sells out, find every live ad still showing it, so I do not send shoppers to something that is gone
jobs.circumstance: The navy 3 pack sold out on Tuesday; 6 live ads still show it on Friday

progress.functional: every live ad that shows an ended offer or a sold-out product, found the day it happens

jobs.hire_today: nothing

forces.push: paid clicks land on a sold-out page
forces.pull: a daily list of live ads tied to ended offers or zero stock
forces.habit: turn off the promo and hope
forces.anxiety: what if it flags ads that show the item only in passing

watch.metric: live ads showing an ended offer or a sold-out product, count, daily
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level, with Shopify inventory and promo dates

drives.metric: spend on those ads, 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6 live ads showing a sold-out pack for 3 days. After: 0 within a day.
jobs.not_for: a store with one product that never sells out or goes on sale

jobs.job: When an ad gets clicks but no sales, check whether the page it lands on is the problem before we kill the ad, so I do not blame the creative for a page fault
jobs.circumstance: A 'no slip heel' ad gets a strong click rate and lands on the home page; sales are poor and the ad is about to be cut

progress.functional: the landing page checked against the ad's promise before the verdict
progress.social: the media buyer and the designer stop blaming each other

jobs.hire_today: nothing; the ad gets cut

forces.push: good ads die for page problems
forces.pull: each ad's page bounce and promise match, next to its verdict
forces.habit: if it does not sell, the ad is bad
forces.anxiety: what if the page and the ad are both weak

watch.metric: bounce rate on the landing page by ad, mobile, 7 days
watch.source: GA4 landing pages by source, with Meta ads

drives.metric: cost per purchase on that ad after a page fix, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the best click ad lands on the home page; bounce 72 percent. After: it lands on the matching product page; bounce 56 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store whose ads all land on one well-matched product page

jobs.job: When an ad is about to be scaled on a product with 2 weeks of stock, warn me, so I do not sell out the winner and waste the audience
jobs.circumstance: A winning ad for the gift box is doubling spend; the gift box has 12 days of stock

progress.functional: ad spend lined up with what is in stock

jobs.hire_today: nothing; ads and stock are run by different people

forces.push: winners sell out and the audience is wasted
forces.pull: stock days next to each ad being scaled
forces.anxiety: what if stock data is late

watch.metric: ad spend on products with under 30 days of stock, share, 7 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level, with Shopify inventory

drives.metric: stockout days on advertised products, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 35 percent of spend on a bundle with 12 days of stock. After: under 10 percent; one ad made for the slowest line.
jobs.not_for: a store that makes to order or never runs low

jobs.job: When most new ads never earn their production cost, raise the share that become winners, so I stop paying for ads that never pay back
jobs.circumstance: 1 in 12 new ads reaches the scale bar, and each one costs $300 to make

progress.functional: a higher share of new ads reaching the scale bar within 14 days

jobs.hire_today: a creative strategist, if there is one
jobs.fire: making more to find the few

forces.push: most production money goes into ads that never pay back
forces.pull: each brief built on a tested angle, with the hit rate tracked by type
forces.anxiety: what if a higher hit rate means safer, duller ads

watch.metric: new ads reaching the scale bar within 14 days of first spend, share, 90 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: creative cost per winning ad, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 in 12 new ads reaches the bar. After: 1 in 7 within a quarter.

jobs.circumstance: The top 3 ads take 78 percent of spend

progress.functional: spend spread across several ideas and formats that each reach different shoppers

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer

forces.push: one tired ad can double costs overnight
forces.pull: the spend mix by idea and format, with the gaps named
forces.anxiety: what if spreading spend lowers results this month

watch.metric: share of spend on the top 3 ads, 7 days

drives.metric: new ad hit rate, 90 days

drives.metric: cost per finished ad, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 usable ads from a $4,000 shoot. After: 20.
jobs.not_for: a store that does not do shoots

jobs.job: When someone says the founder should be in the ads, tell me if my face actually sells or if a customer would do better, so I do not spend days on camera for nothing
jobs.circumstance: The agency wants 4 founder videos a month, and the founder dreads filming

progress.functional: founder ads read against the same script with a customer or creator
progress.emotional: stop the dread of filming for nothing

jobs.hire_today: the agency's advice and gut
jobs.fire: filming because the agency said so

forces.push: days on camera with no proof it sells
forces.pull: a side by side test of founder against customer on the same script
forces.anxiety: what if the test says my face does not sell

watch.metric: cost per purchase, founder ads against the same script with a customer, 14 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: founder hours on filming per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 founder shoots a month, value unknown. After: 1 a month, with customer videos in the rest.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no founder story or a founder who loves filming

jobs.job: When an ad wins on Meta, get it onto TikTok, YouTube and our own social without starting over, so I earn from one proven idea everywhere
jobs.circumstance: A winning Meta video has never run anywhere else

progress.functional: each winning idea adapted for other channels in their own style

jobs.hire_today: an editor rebuilding it from scratch, or nothing

forces.push: proven ideas earn in only one place
forces.pull: a list of winners not yet run elsewhere, with what each needs
forces.habit: each channel needs its own ads
forces.anxiety: what if it looks like a Meta ad on TikTok

watch.metric: Meta winners adapted for at least one other channel, share
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, ad level, with the creative log

drives.metric: cost per purchase on other channels, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 of 8 winners run elsewhere. After: 5 of 8; 2 win on TikTok.
jobs.not_for: a store that advertises on one channel only

jobs.job: When one ad brings buyers who return more or never reorder, catch it before we scale it, so I do not make the cheapest sale the most costly customer
jobs.circumstance: The cheapest-cost ad brings buyers who return 18 percent of orders

progress.functional: each ad judged on the buyers it brings over 60 days, not just the first order

jobs.hire_today: nothing
jobs.fire: judging ads on first order cost alone

forces.push: cheap ads can bring costly buyers
forces.pull: returns and reorders by the ad that brought the buyer
forces.habit: cost per purchase is the score
forces.anxiety: what if tracking buyers to ads is too rough

watch.metric: return rate and 60 day repeat rate of buyers by first ad, 60 days
watch.source: Shopify orders and returns with UTM source, and Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: gross profit per new customer by ad, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the cheapest ad's buyers return 18 percent of orders. After: caught before scaling; spend moved to an ad whose buyers return 6 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store with too few orders to split buyers by ad

jobs.job: When a creator's permission or a music license is about to end on a live ad, tell me before the date, so I do not get the ad taken down or claimed
jobs.circumstance: 3 live ads use creator videos whose permission ends in 2 weeks

progress.functional: every right on a live ad with its end date and a warning

jobs.hire_today: nothing

forces.push: a live ad taken down mid-scale
forces.pull: a rights list with dates and owners
forces.habit: we will sort it if they ask
forces.anxiety: what if renewing costs more than the ad earns

watch.metric: live ads with a right or permission ending in 30 days, count
watch.source: creative rights log, with Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: live ads pulled for a rights issue, 12 months

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 live ads with permission ending in 2 weeks. After: renewed or replaced before the date.
jobs.not_for: a store that uses only its own footage and music

jobs.job: When I wonder what rivals are testing that we are not, show me the formats and angles they lean on as ideas to try, never to copy, so I do not miss a shift in the feed
jobs.circumstance: Three rivals all started running side by side comparison ads last month

progress.functional: rival formats and angles run widely that we have not tried in 90 days

jobs.hire_today: a creative strategist now and then, or scrolling rival pages

forces.push: shifts in the feed are seen late
forces.pull: a short list of gaps to test with our own claims and footage
forces.anxiety: what if rival ads are not working and we copy a loser

watch.metric: formats or angles run by 3 or more rivals that we have not tried in 90 days, count
watch.source: Meta Ad Library, with Meta Ads Manager, ad level

drives.metric: new ad hit rate from gap tests, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 open gaps, including comparison ads. After: 2 tested in the next month with our own claims and footage.
jobs.not_for: a brand in a category with no active rival advertisers
